section_summary: This section records requests and interdepartmental replies concerning Japanese transports visiting California ports in 1941 to load crude petroleum. As the visits became more frequent, the Navy questioned whether commercial tankers carrying naval personnel should receive the privileges of public naval vessels. The section also records the Erimo’s arrival at San Francisco after permission had been sought for Los Angeles, and a later distinction between commercial vessels and bona fide warships.

subfiles.about: Treatment of Japanese special naval transports.
